tasks.commitBody:
An id coerced to '' composes 'entity/', which entu-api resolves to
the entity LIST route — answering 200 with a benign-looking empty
result instead of an error. That shape produced two silent
failures on this board: #255's rights guard reading 'no grants
held' from a check that never ran, and the library resolving blank
copy names and chains from lending rows with missing references.
A sweep found 53 entity-composition sites: three reachable-empty
(all from one pair of '?? '' defaults), six guarded, and 44 safe
only by tracing — an invariant living in callers' heads, which is
exactly how it fell out twice.

Two fixes, deliberately in one change. The root cause: lending
rows no longer default missing copy/member references to '' — the
malformed row is handled visibly per the stated choice in the
review record, and the date defaults beside them stay, since dates
never compose into a path. The class: the request layer now
refuses to send any path whose entity segment ends with no id —
loudly, before the network, with an error naming the composition.
A trailing 'entity/' is never legitimate (verified: every such
occurrence in the repo is a spec asserting URLs), so the guard
breaks nothing and converts 44 traced-safe sites into
structurally-safe ones. It also catches, at the point of use, the
three assumptions the sweep could not verify — which stay recorded
on the issue, deliberately unresolved.

The intentional list query ('entity?...', no slash) and every
legitimate single-entity read are byte-unaffected, pinned by
negative tests. #255's own fail-closed guard stays as the first
net; this is the second, beneath every caller.

Live gate (Mihkel): none user-visible by design — the payoff is
the next empty-id bug failing loudly at composition instead of
shipping a silent blank.
